newsitem.title: EGYPT: Islamic Group denies responsibility for massacre.
newsitem.headline: Islamic Group denies responsibility for massacre.

text.p: Egypt's main Islamist militant group said on Saturday it had nothing to do with an attack on Thursday in which gunmen killed 13 people near the southern town of Naga Hammadi.
The al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) said in a faxed statement that a branch of the Egyptian security forces may have organised the attack to discredit the Islamists.
Police have said they suspect the Gama'a and have named three Gama'a members they say are suspects.
Police also suspect the Gama'a carried out an attack in which gunmen killed eight young Coptic Christians last month in a youth meeting in the southern town of Abu Qurqas.
But the Gama'a statement said: "Just as the Gama'a denied responsibility for the incidents of the Copts, it also denies responsibility for the Naga Hammadi incident."

"The Gama'a has affirmed in the past that its operations adhere to the rules of sharia (Islamic law), even with non- Moslems, and that its conflict is with the Egyptian regime, represented in its leaders and supporters," it added.

"Just as our previous statements did not rule out the Egyptian security apparatus being involved in the incident of the Copts, based on the information available to us we now affirm that there are suspicious quarters, foreign and local, behind the planning of these incidents," it said.

"It's no secret to anyone that there are bitter conflicts between trends inside the Egyptian political establishment... Perhaps the same quarters have aspirations to tarnish the image of Islamists in Egypt, as they have in Algeria," it added.
More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence since the militants took up arms in 1992 to topple the government of President Hosni Mubarak.
